name: Hallucination Detector
description: Compare generated content claims against original source material to flag statements that aren't supported by any source.
usage_notes: Run after content-writer has produced content_markdown and page-scraper/browser-scraper has produced text_content. Grades only the LATEST content_markdown draft (.at(-1), matching the step-8 output modules). Uses LLM to verify each factual claim against source material. If no source text_content is available, the entity FAILS closed by default (unverifiable is not verified) -- set no_sources_behavior to soften. Substantial content that yields zero extractable claims also fails closed (padding-blind signature); the regex extractor cannot see qualitative claims (coverage gap tracked as UNIT_50 #51). SOURCE SELECTION (U1): by default (source_selection='head') the source window is the corpus HEAD truncated at max_source_chars -- on a fat entity (600k+ char corpus) the supporting page is often BEYOND the window, so its claim is flagged as a truncation artifact. Set source_selection='claim_anchored' to build a per-batch window from the source chunks whose terms overlap the batch's claims (deterministic, no extra LLM call); claim_anchored also emits honest-window meta (source_corpus_chars, source_chars_shown, evidence_in_window/beyond_window/absent) so a truncation-driven verdict is distinguishable from a real fabrication. COST (v1.4.0, MODEL_SCREEN Screen 5; acceptance measured on run 94baa6f6, 2026-09-03 -- detector is 36.7% of per-entity cost, the single largest line): (Unit A) claim EXTRACTION (claim_extraction='llm') is parsing-grade, so extraction_model/extraction_provider let it run on a cheaper model (default null = inherit verification model, byte-identical). The VERIFICATION model (ai_model) is the referee that grades every module -- always leave it on sonnet. NOTE (acceptance): the Screen-5 candidate openai/gpt-oss-120b FAILED the +-15% claim-count parity gate when measured N=3 on ELK/PRG/Vermantia -- it under-extracts by -12% to -56% (median -13% / -47% / -36%) with high variance, so it checks materially FEWER claims than sonnet. It DOES still read table/list claims (table facts present in every draw), just at coarser granularity. Do NOT route extraction to gpt-oss-120b in production on this evidence; the ~$90/1,700 Unit A saving is not safe until a cheaper model passes the parity gate (haiku is banned on this long-document read). The option ships as a generic mechanism; validate claim-count parity per candidate model before use. (Unit B) cache_base_window=true reuses the stable base (head) source window across an entity's verification batches via an Anthropic cache_prefix instead of re-sending it every batch. ACCEPTANCE PASSED (N=3 ELK/PRG, N=2 Vermantia): cache_read>0 on batches>=2 every draw; verification-cost reduction 27% (ELK, 2 batches) / 51% (PRG, 3) / 65% (Vermantia, 5) on the cold first draw, scaling with batch count; and verdict PARITY vs the deployed single-prompt baseline held (ELK/Vermantia still FAIL their genuine fabrications, PRG still PASSES; scores within the jitter band). ~$0.132/entity (~$224/1,700). Default false = byte-identical. Anthropic-only (non-anthropic providers ignore cache_prefix and fall back to the single prompt). VERIFICATION-FAILURE DISCIPLINE (v1.7.0): an unverified claim is NOT an unsupported claim. If any verification request fails or is never run (rate limit, network blip, refused call), the entity HARD-FAILS as an INFRASTRUCTURE failure -- meta.status:'error', error:'verification_incomplete', with failed_batches/batches_not_attempted/claims_unverified on meta -- and is retried by the skeleton, never flagged as content. No claim from a failed batch is ever reported 'unsupported', the score never moves because of a call that did not happen, and severity_floor never trips on a claim nobody examined. (Before v1.7.0 the sync path degraded failed batches to verdict:'unsupported': the offering-slot draw-2 incident turned 2 budget-refused batches into hallucination 0.495 + a spurious QA FAIL on a fully corpus-grounded draft. Fourth instance of the infra-failure-reported-as-content-finding family; ENGINEERING_CONTRACT section 5.) Sync also stops calling remaining batches after the first failure -- their results would be discarded on retry, so further spend is waste. TOP-K RETRIEVAL + REPAIRED in_window INSTRUMENT (v1.8.0): claim_anchored's supplement previously pulled only the SINGLE best IDF-ranked chunk per claim -- a decoy chunk sharing many generic terms with the claim outranked the short page actually stating the fact, so the true support was never shown (23 of 27 audited flags in validation run 9821ed56; ~30 of 43 flags were corpus-true false positives) and a best-scoring HEAD chunk suppressed the supplement entirely. v1.8.0 pulls each claim's TOP-5 candidate chunks (K=5 = the knee of the measured rank-coverage curve on the 27-specimen set; possessive stems and digit-led tokens repaired in term extraction: 'SoftSwiss's' now matches 'SoftSwiss', '1X2' is no longer dropped), filled by rank tier so a deeper nomination never crowds out another claim's best chunk; the supplement budget is unchanged (<= max_source_chars on top of the head). The in_window label previously credited ANY selected chunk sharing ANY single discriminating term -- a decoy satisfied it, so all 43 flags of run 9821ed56 read in_window while their evidence sat beyond the window, and the broken label concealed the retrieval defect for the whole validation run. It now means: ALL of the claim's top-K candidate chunks were shown (retrieval exhausted its lexical candidates -- trust the flag); beyond_window = at least one candidate was not shown (possible retrieval artifact -- retry/review); absent = no lexical trace anywhere (candidate fabrication; unchanged, load-bearing for severity_model=evidence_absent). WELD SEVERITY RULE (v1.8.0, code-locked prompt): a claim that pairs real elements in a way the sources CONTRADICT (city under the wrong country, award under the wrong product/year, fact on the wrong subject) grades unsupported/high on the EVIDENCE. Before top-K, this class ('Malaga, Sweden') was caught only when retrieval FAILED to show the claim's evidence -- the same blindness that false-flagged corpus-true claims -- so any retrieval improvement softened it (the refused max_source_chars=300k raise dropped it HIGH->MEDIUM; measured again under top-K without this rule: partial/medium). With the rule: unsupported/HIGH on 4/4 fixed-claim draws WITH the evidence shown, while corpus-absent controls (Halcyon-$240M, Quasar-Turnip, Danske-Spil weld) stay HIGH and aggregation claims (offices lists, multi-region expansion unions) are NOT escalated -- the rule requires contradiction, not mere absence of the stated pairing. SEVERITY-FLOOR CONFIRMATION (v1.9.0, option floor_confirmation, default false = byte-identical): THE DEFECT -- with severity_floor=true a draft fails if ANY single claim grades unsupported/HIGH. A rich profile carries 150-200 claims, and at 25 claims/batch the shared window budget caps each claim's effective top-K at 1-2 chunks, so at production volume something corpus-true grades HIGH on most draws (retrieval starvation, not fabrication): run 9821ed56 measured auto-approve 1/6 with 13 of 16 floor HIGHs corpus-true FPs, unchanged by the v1.8.0 retrieval fix because small-batch gains do not survive full-batch contention. THE INSTRUMENT LIMIT -- the v1.8.0 repaired in_window tag made this measurable but CANNOT gate the floor: at full volume genuine fabrications read beyond_window exactly like the FPs (measured: Malaga/Sweden, BetMGM 17-Aug, the GBP-50m program, and all three injected corpus-absent controls), while the few in_window tags sit on FPs -- an evidence-gated floor would be INVERTED (pass the fabrications, keep blocking the FPs) and was refused; likewise severity_model=evidence_absent remains weld-unsafe. THE MECHANISM -- when the floor trips, the floor-tripping HIGH claims are re-verified in batches of <=8 (uncontended retrieval: full top-K per claim) through the SAME verifier and code-locked prompt (incl. the weld rule); the floor stands only on a claim that re-verifies at severity HIGH. Release is SEVERITY-gated, not verdict-gated: a claim re-verifying 'partial' but still HIGH keeps blocking (measured on the BC GBP50m/EUR50m currency error -- substance true, currency false -- partial/HIGH on 2/2 small-batch draws; a verdict-gated release would let it escape). Severity is NEVER regraded from an evidence tag; the only release is the verifier affirmatively grading below HIGH. FAIL-CLOSED: an errored confirmation call, unparseable response, or missing verdict CONFIRMS those claims (the main verification completed, so this is a content verdict, not an infra failure). A released floor decides on the EXACT unrounded threshold; ALL flags are retained with floor_confirmed per HIGH plus meta.floor_confirmation {highs_initial, highs_confirmed, highs_cleared, batches, claims[{claim,confirmed,verdict,severity,evidence}]}. Sync-only: execution_mode=batch ignores it with a warning (all-or-nothing floor kept -- conservative). ACCEPTANCE (measured 2026-09-19, v1.9.0 end-to-end on the six frozen entities of run 9821ed56): every known fabrication still blocks -- Malaga/Sweden CONFIRMED unsupported/high end-to-end + HIGH 6/6 small-batch draws; BetMGM 17-Aug CONFIRMED end-to-end + 2/2 fixed; Dinopolis award weld CONFIRMED end-to-end + 2/2 fixed; GBP50m partial/HIGH 2/2 fixed (blocks via the severity gate); injected Danske-Spil/Halcyon/Quasar HIGH 3/3 fixed draws each and the injected-draft end-to-end run stays blocked (at full production volume the main pass grades Danske+Halcyon unsupported/HIGH and Quasar unsupported/MEDIUM -- flagged, byte-matching the pre-option baseline, which also never floor-tripped Quasar at full volume). Auto-approve before->after on the same draws: 0/6 -> 1/6 (iGP recovered: 6/6 FP HIGHs cleared with affirmative verdicts, PASS at 0.897 with flags retained). The remaining blocks are majority-GENUINE (LeoVegas F6+F7; Push Dinopolis + a corpus-absent incorporation-day precision; PayRetailers Kuady-ownership x2 analyzer world-knowledge insertions; Vixio draw-dependent genuine-'former CEO'/FP-flicker; BC = the residual FP class: one stable deep-retrieval-miss (PariuriX) + two subject-attribution welds). Confirmed-HIGH precision: 3/16 genuine (19%) under the unconfirmed floor -> ~6-8/11 (55-73%) confirmed. The floor is calibrated; auto-approve VOLUME is now bounded upstream by analyzer-origin defect density (F-E date-precision, F-F cite-or-null classes), not by floor noise. COST: one extra <=8-claim sonnet call per floor-tripping entity, ~$0.08-0.12 with cache_base_window (the cached base window re-reads at 10%). EXTRACTION TRUNCATION GUARD (v1.10.0): THE DEFECT -- the claim-EXTRACTION call (claim_extraction='llm') inherited ai.complete's 16384 default max_tokens. On a heavy draw (a rich profile's 150-200 claims PLUS sonnet-5's adaptive thinking, which is ON when 'thinking' is omitted and bills against the SAME output cap) the extraction JSON truncated, became unparseable, and the module silently FELL BACK to the regex extractor (~4 claims on a v3 draft) -> the severity floor never tripped -> qa_pass:true. This is the SEVENTH instance of this codebase's worst failure family and the FIRST that fails OPEN: a fabricated profile could publish. Same class as the analyzer output ceiling (content-pipeline-specs template-v3/ceiling/CEILING.md); different model, different number. THE FIX (both halves): (1) the extraction call now passes an explicit max_tokens = 65536 (CODE-LOCKED constant EXTRACTION_MAX_TOKENS, not a template option -- a template must not lower it back into the hole). sonnet-5's real output ceiling is 131072 and the deployed draws emit only 4-7k extraction tokens for the fattest (200-claim) entity, so 65536 is ~4x the observed worst case plus room for the non-deterministic thinking tail; the adapter (stageWorker + buildBatchRequestParams) streams and forwards max_tokens unclamped, so it is safe from HTTP timeouts. (2) a truncated extraction can no longer become a regex fallback that produces a verdict: it HARD-FAILS the entity as an INFRA failure (meta.status:'error', error:'extraction_truncated', qa_pass:false, needs_review:true) -- the same v1.7.0 discipline that already covers failed verification batches -- so a degraded extraction can NEVER yield qa_pass:true. Two truncation signals: stop_reason=='max_tokens' (definitive; present in SYNC), and a NON-EMPTY response that does not parse to a claim array (the only trace in BATCH mode, where the skeleton strips stop_reason). PRESERVED byte-identical: a NORMAL extraction (sync AND batch), an ERRORED call (still regex fallback -- a transient blip), and a genuine empty [] (still regex fallback -> the H21 zero-claims guard). Banked run 9821ed56: all 6 entities extracted at end_turn (0 truncations in that committed run); the false pass is a non-deterministic re-draw tail -- this guard eliminates it whichever way it fires.

options.name: pass_threshold
options.label: Pass threshold
options.description: Minimum hallucination_score (0-1) for qa_pass to be true. 1.0 means every claim must be verified.

options.name: ai_model
options.label: AI Model
options.description: Which model to use for claim verification.

options.name: max_source_chars
options.label: Max source characters
options.description: Maximum total characters of source text to include in LLM context. Truncates oldest sources first if exceeded.

options.name: claims_per_batch
options.label: Claims per batch
options.description: Number of claims to verify in each LLM call. Higher values use fewer API calls but risk hitting context limits.

options.name: allow_empty_content
options.label: Allow empty content
options.description: When true, an entity with no content_markdown skips with a pass (nothing to verify). When false (default), missing content fails closed -- content was expected but is absent, and a QA gate must not certify content it never read.

options.name: no_sources_behavior
options.label: Behavior when no sources
options.description: What to do when there is NO source text_content to verify against. 'fail' (default) fails closed -- content asserting claims with nothing to ground them against is unverifiable, and unverifiable is not verified. 'flag' passes but marks needs_review. 'pass' restores the legacy skip-with-pass for pipelines that legitimately have no sources.

options.name: flag_zero_claims_over_chars
options.label: Zero-claims fail threshold (chars)
options.description: When claim extraction returns ZERO claims, content longer than this (chars) fails closed -- long content with no extractable claim is the padding-blind signature (all-qualitative content the regex extractor cannot see). Shorter no-claim content is a low-confidence pass (needs_review). Calibration knob: measure the trip rate; do not dial down to silence a genuine halt.

options.name: claim_extraction
options.label: Claim extraction strategy
options.description: How factual claims are pulled from the draft before verification. 'regex' (default) keeps only enumerated numeric/date/company sentences in prose -- fast, zero cost, but blind to facts placed in markdown tables and lists. 'llm' runs a code-locked extraction pass over the FULL draft (prose + tables + lists), restoring claim granularity on formats that move facts into Quick-Facts tables. The verification stage is unchanged; only extraction differs. LLM mode adds one LLM call per entity.

options.name: severity_floor
options.label: High-severity fabrication force-fails
options.description: When true, any claim verified as unsupported AND rated high-severity (a specific fabricated number, date, statistic, or financial claim) force-fails the check regardless of the numeric score -- closing the '1 hard fabrication in 10 claims = exactly 0.9 = pass' hole. The score still reports the honest ratio; only qa_pass is forced false, emitted through the same hallucination:fail routing key (no new key). Default false preserves pure-threshold behavior.

options.name: severity_model
options.label: Severity model (for the floor)
options.description: Which severity gates severity_floor. 'current' (default, byte-identical) uses the LLM's raw high/medium/low. 'evidence_absent' reserves HIGH for claims whose SUBJECT is absent from the corpus entirely: a high unsupported claim whose evidence IS present (evidence_in_window or beyond_window) is a grounded fact with an over-claimed qualifier (superlative/absolute/over-extension), not a fabrication, so it is regraded to MEDIUM and the floor does not force-fail it -- while a claim with no source anywhere STAYS high and still force-fails. Only severity is regraded; the supported/unsupported verdict and the score are never changed. Requires source_selection='claim_anchored' to classify evidence (in 'head' mode there is nothing to classify against, so nothing is regraded -- a warning is logged). Use when the floor is firing on grounded facts that carry one over-claimed qualifier rather than on genuine fabrications: those pass but still ship their claims in the published qa_flags for review.

options.name: floor_confirmation
options.label: Confirm floor HIGHs by re-verification
options.description: When true (with severity_floor), a tripped floor does not block immediately: the floor-tripping HIGH claims are re-verified in a small focused batch (uncontended retrieval -- each claim gets its full top-K supplement), and the floor stands only on a HIGH that survives re-verification. Clears the retrieval-starvation FP class that blocks clean 150-200-claim profiles (validation run 9821ed56: 13 of 16 floor HIGHs were corpus-true FPs; auto-approve 1/6) while genuine fabrications re-verify HIGH and still block (measured: Malaga/Sweden weld and the three injected corpus-absent controls stay HIGH on every small-batch draw). Severity is never regraded from an evidence tag; the only release path is the same verifier + code-locked prompt affirmatively grading the claim below unsupported/HIGH. Fail-closed: an errored confirmation call, unparseable response, or missing verdict keeps those claims blocking. A released floor hands the decision back to the score (pass_threshold untouched); ALL flags are retained for review with floor_confirmed true/false per HIGH plus meta.floor_confirmation counts. Sync-only: in execution_mode=batch it is ignored with a warning (all-or-nothing floor kept -- conservative). Default false = byte-identical current behaviour.

options.name: source_selection
options.label: Source selection strategy
options.description: How the source window sent to the verifier is built. 'head' (default) concatenates pages in pool order and truncates at max_source_chars -- byte-identical to prior behaviour, but on a fat entity (600k+ char corpus) the supporting page is frequently BEYOND the window, so its claim is flagged 'unsupported' as a pure truncation artifact. 'claim_anchored' sends the full head window PLUS a supplement of the best IDF-ranked far chunks for claims the head misses -- so the window is up to ~2x max_source_chars (still far cheaper than a full-corpus raise) and can never regress an entity whose evidence is already in the head. It emits honest-window meta (source_corpus_chars, source_chars_shown, evidence_in_window/beyond_window/absent) that distinguishes a truncation artifact from a real fabrication. NOTE: because claim_anchored can roughly double the payload, set max_source_chars with ~2x headroom against the model's context limit. To measure a raw window-raise instead, keep 'head' and increase max_source_chars.

options.name: extraction_model
options.label: Claim-extraction model (Unit A)
options.description: Model for the claim-EXTRACTION call only (claim_extraction='llm'). Extraction is parsing-grade and can run cheaper than verification. Empty/null (default) inherits ai_model -- byte-identical to today. WARNING: the Screen-5 candidate openrouter/gpt-oss-120b FAILED the +-15% claim-count parity gate on measurement (N=3, 2026-09-03): it under-extracts -12% to -56% (fewer claims checked). Do NOT use it in production. Any cheaper extraction model must first be validated for claim-count parity vs the sonnet extractor. Has NO effect on verification -- ai_model still grades every claim.

options.name: extraction_provider
options.label: Claim-extraction provider (Unit A)
options.description: Provider for the claim-EXTRACTION call only. Empty/null (default) inherits ai_provider. Set alongside extraction_model (e.g. 'openrouter' with 'gpt-oss-120b'). Verification provider (ai_provider) is unchanged.

options.name: cache_base_window
options.label: Cache base source window across batches (Unit B)
options.description: When true, the stable base (head) source window shared by all of an entity's verification batches is sent once as an Anthropic prompt cache_prefix and re-read at ~10% input cost on later batches, instead of being re-sent in full every batch (measured redundancy 24-60% per entity). The verifier sees the SAME instructions, sources and claims -- only the section order changes (sources before claims), and verdict parity to the single-prompt path is the acceptance gate. Default false = byte-identical single prompt. Anthropic-only: non-anthropic verification providers ignore cache_prefix, so the split falls back to the single prompt for them (never drops the base window). Best paired with source_selection='claim_anchored', which is where the base is the fixed head window.

options.name: execution_mode
options.label: Execution mode
options.description: How the LLM calls run. 'sync' (default) executes each extraction + verification call synchronously, one entity at a time, exactly as before -- byte-identical. 'batch' opts this step into the Anthropic Message Batches path (skeleton-driven): all the step's entities are collected and submitted as two Message Batches (round 1 extractions, round 2 verifications), billed at 50% of standard, with an async return (results typically <1h, up to 24h). Verdicts are unchanged -- only WHEN the result arrives and the billing rate differ. Anthropic-only (the batch path requires ai_provider=anthropic). In BOTH modes a failed/expired/never-run verification request fails that entity loudly as an infrastructure error (meta.status:'error' -- retried, never a silent pass, never a content verdict; v1.7.0). Rollback is a config flip back to 'sync', not a code revert.
